findings.reason: the plan's whole justification and §9's comparison rest on a record that does not exist, so the author must either author it or cite the one that holds these numbers.

findings.reason: §9's deliverable is defined against a figure that is not in the tree, so its write path and its redraw instruction name work against nothing.

findings.reason: two nodes would repair one reflex independently, and §8 also omits the measured cause §28 already established, so the wiring and the root cause both change.
findings.text: §1's exclusion map claims this plan takes only costs no other plan owns, but `the-monitor-reads-each-fact-once` §28 "A slow station refresh does not hold the review reflex" owns exactly §8's problem, with four measured cases of reviews launched 6-10 min after delivery against a 120 s window; §8 declares no depends-on or informs edge to it

findings.reason: the declared wait is right but the prose reports it satisfied, so a coordinator reading the text would dispatch §7 against an unmet upstream and two plans would carry the same pass-latency target at different bounds.
findings.text: §7 states `work-flows-to-the-lane` §77 "is delivered", but §77's own record carries `data-status="implementable"` (unmet), and §77's title claims the same quantity this section bounds, "An admission pass fills the free slots within a minute"

findings.reason: the clause makes §4's gate fail or pass on another plan's deliverable, so it must either become a declared dependency or leave §4's done-when.
findings.text: §4's second measure, "a fully unchanged, unexpired pass ... performs no input read and returns in under 0.1 s", is the read-reuse cost `the-monitor-reads-each-fact-once` §25 "The station's fleet refresh reuses its reads between ticks" and §13 own; §4 declares no edge to that plan

findings.reason: a done-when that cannot fail measures nothing, so a fleet-wide miss would close the plan's final section as success without any verdict on the §2–§8 bounds.
findings.text: §9's gate holds regardless of outcome: "A measure that misses its bound is reported with the stage that caused it, and that is a complete result", so the node closes as delivered whether every bound is met or none is

findings.reason: the receipt is a prerequisite deliverable whose result decides whether the 20 s bound is reachable, so the node either splits or its bound becomes conditional on the measurement.
findings.text: §7 asks for two things in one node: admission receipts that name each release and wait read with its time, and a pass that decides within 20 s, while §85 says those two stages "have not been profiled, so their cause is not known"

findings.reason: a cause the plan's data does not support, already measured in `the-monitor-reads-each-fact-once` §28, sends §8's repair at a mechanism nobody has shown to be the one costing 17.5 minutes.
findings.text: §8's mechanism is asserted against its own evidence: §1's table records the review-launch delay as "not established" (plan.html:44), yet §8's negative control says "at the base the review is not requested until the held tick ends", which claims the tick is the cause and would pass even if the real delay lies elsewhere
